title: Filtered Indexes
description: Learn how to create filtered indexes to optimize queries on a subset of rows.

data.text: A filtered index is a nonclustered index with a predicate that allows you to specify which rows should be added to the index. This is useful when applications query only a portion of rows in a table.

data.title: CREATE INDEX with WHERE clause
data.content: Creates a filtered index for phone numbers that are not null.

data.text: The phone column in the sales.customers table contains many NULL values. A filtered index on non-null phone values is more efficient than a full index on the column:

data.title: Filtered Index on phone column
data.content: Creates a filtered index for customers with non-null phone numbers.

items: Save storage space especially when index key columns are sparse (many NULL values).
Reduce maintenance cost because only a portion of data rows need to be updated.
Improve query performance for queries that filter on the predicate condition.

data.text: Making the Optimizer Use the Filter

The optimizer only uses a filtered index when it can prove the query cannot need rows outside the filter. A literal predicate usually works; a parameterised one may not, because the value is unknown at compile time. The script below builds a filtered index and confirms it exists in metadata.

data.title: Filtered index on a sparse column
data.content: This index is small because it contains only the rows where phone is present.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE #Customers (
    customer_id INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    email NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    phone NVARCHAR(25) NULL
);

CREATE INDEX ix_cust_phone ON #Customers (phone)
    WHERE phone IS NOT NULL;

-- Uses the filtered index: the predicate exactly implies the filter
SELECT customer_id
FROM #Customers
WHERE phone IS NOT NULL;

SELECT
    name,
    has_filter,
    filter_definition
FROM tempdb.sys.indexes
WHERE object_id = OBJECT_ID('tempdb..#Customers') AND has_filter = 1;

data.title: Filtered index gotchas
data.text: A filtered index cannot be used if the query uses `OR`, `NOT IN`, `IS NULL` variants that contradict the filter, or a parameter whose value is not known at compile time. For those cases, add the parameter to the session with `OPTION (RECOMPILE)` or rewrite the predicate. Also remember that a filtered index cannot enforce a constraint across rows that are excluded by the filter.

data.title: Filtered Index Key Points
points: Filtered indexes are nonclustered indexes with a WHERE predicate.
They are ideal for columns with many NULL values or sparse data.
They reduce both storage and maintenance overhead compared to full indexes.
The query optimizer can leverage filtered indexes when the WHERE clause matches the predicate.
